tldr: For every fixed binary potential-outcome table, the causal target is the finite-SATE and exactly \(m\) of \(n\) labels are treated uniformly. The full-record minimax squared error is \(R_n(m)=V_p/n-C_AV_p^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o_K(n^{-4/3})\), with \(p=m/n\) and \(V_p=1/(4p(1-p))\), uniformly over all interior integer allocations. A total clipped nonlinear action and a certified rational approximation attain this expansion. Comparison with the published free-design minimax value proves that every quota with \(|m_n-n/2|=o(n^{5/6})\), together with the explicit action, is globally minimax through second order. Writing \(\delta_n=m_n/n-1/2\), if \(n^{1/6}\delta_n\to\xi\), both risks have scaled excess tending to \(4\xi^2\); if \(\delta_n\to0\) and \(n^{1/6}|\delta_n|\to\infty\), both excesses are asymptotic to \(4\delta_n^2/n\). Thus \(n^{5/6}\) is the exact count-imbalance elbow near half allocation. The uniform comparison also quantifies both orders of the penalty at every fixed interior unequal quota.
